Line numbers in these panes are shifted by this banner, which Compiler Explorer
prepends to the source before compiling, so compare positions rather than the
numbers quoted elsewhere.

The source has one statement before a #line directive and one after it. This is
a compute restating of the pixel-shader repro that was measured locally; Clang's
DXIL backend cannot lower a shader writing SV_Target, and the two DXC panes are
the control that the restating still shows the behaviour under test.

Panes 1 and 2 (dxcompiler, oldest available and trunk): look at the !DILocation
nodes near the end. Both statements are described by physical positions in this
file, and every !DIFile names this file. The name the directive gives appears
only inside !dx.source.contents, which is the compiler echoing the source back,
not a debug location.

Pane 3 is the same trunk compiler emitting SPIR-V from the same source, and pane
4 is the Clang-based HLSL front end emitting DXIL. Both do the opposite: the
statement after the directive is attributed to the file the directive names.

Compiler Explorer's oldest DXC is 1.6.2112, which is already past the change
this issue is about, so no pane here shows dxcompiler's earlier behaviour.
